clue.text: What tidy clues about dead former yuppie for Morse!

definitions.text: What tidy clues about dead former yuppie for Morse!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters are wrapped round what follows
to clue (or clew) is to wind yarn into a ball, so the word before it is wound up and its letters jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled
D is the standard abbreviation for dead
a yump was an early-1980s term for a young upwardly mobile professional, the forerunner of the yuppie

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a neat puzzle about a dead yuppie, written for Inspector Morse to crack.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: the result is the stuff Morse code is made of. 'Clues' is Chambers' verb for winding into a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Iddy-umpty is a jocular name for Morse code signalling, imitating the sound of its dots and dashes.

clue.text: Slight suspicion on entering liquid measure

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first word is placed within the measure

parts.note: the bath was a Hebrew measure of liquid capacity
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A hint of doubt arises while measuring out a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: The bath is the ancient Hebrew liquid measure, about eight gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath of scandal or suspicion is a faint hint or trace of it.

clue.text: They enable crustacean to sense mate on half of upturned ship

indicators.note: half of a word means keeping only one of its two halves and dropping the rest
in a down entry, on means placed above, so one part sits on top of the next

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate

indicators.note: in a down clue upturned means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the second half of the word ship

explanation.surface: A crustacean feels for a mate on the hull of a capsized ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpi are the jointed feelers near the mouth of arthropods, used as sense organs.

clue.text: Special snack bar service following rubbish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
a caff is British slang for a cheap café
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A special café service follows some rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is a cheap British café; following gives F as in 'pp. 10 f.'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaff-raff is an old dialect variant of riff-raff, meaning worthless people or refuse.

clue.text: Company supported by food climbing ridges

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported means sitting on top of the other part

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: A firm relies on food that is climbing in price or popularity.
explanation.definitionFit: Costae are ribs, and in botany and zoology the term covers rib-like ridges.

clue.text: Resistance to heat making the canary flutter round head of mine

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters are placed around the single letter
to flutter is to flap about restlessly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of mine

explanation.surface: A canary flutters around a mine, the old warning bird of the coal pits.
explanation.definitionFit: Athermancy is the property of being impervious to radiant heat, a technical term from physics.

clue.text: Zap, using loud artillery grenades initially

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
the RA is the Royal Artillery

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: first letter of grenades

explanation.surface: Someone blasts a target with noisy artillery and grenades.
explanation.definitionFit: To frag is military slang for attacking someone with a fragmentation grenade, so to zap or kill them.

clue.text: Worried re fatal cause of verminous infestation

indicators.note: worried in its old sense of shaken and mauled about, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about something deadly that spreads vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat flea is the parasite of rats that infests them and carried bubonic plague to people.

clue.text: Once dejected, penning English love poem

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the outer word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: amort is an obsolete word for spiritless or dejected
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A once gloomy writer composes an English love poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Amort, an old word for lifeless or downcast, is what 'Once dejected' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoret is a love sonnet or love song, from the French for a little love.

clue.text: Last and first of file in a line

indicators.note: first of a word means only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of file
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Someone is told the last and first entries of a file arranged in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Final means coming at the end, the same as last.

clue.text: Sort of lizard Jack maybe flipped over

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a jack is an example of a playing card
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A lizard, perhaps one called Jack, gets flipped onto its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack maybe' looks like a lizard's name but is a playing card. In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco is the genus of flying lizards of South-East Asia, which glide on skin flaps.

clue.text: Member of famous trio, artist appearing in cloak

indicators.note: appearing in means showing up inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: amis is an old form of amice, a cloak or hood
an RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: One of a well-known trio turns up dressed in an artist's cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: Amis, a variant of amice, is a hooded cape worn by clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramis is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, alongside Athos and Porthos.

clue.text: Yummy wing in what's served for dinner?

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

parts.note: a dish is a course served at a meal
an el is an extension or wing of a building, especially an L-shaped one

explanation.surface: A tasty chicken wing appears in the dinner being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wing' suggests chicken, but it is a building's wing, an el.
explanation.definitionFit: Delish is a colloquial shortening of delicious, as is yummy.

clue.text: Intellectual ability

parts.note: the surface reading: a capacity for thinking
the setter's reading: this is the competition clue, printed as a bare definition for solvers to write their own clue

explanation.walkthrough: This is the Azed competition entry: the puzzle prints only a definition, and entrants invent the wordplay themselves, so there is no wordplay to parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainpower is mental capacity or intelligence, the capacity to think and reason well.

clue.text: An old fool, displaying lack of energy

parts.note: the indefinite article in its short form
tony is an obsolete word for a simpleton or fool

explanation.surface: An elderly fool shows signs of running out of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: Atony is a medical term for weakness or lack of normal tone, slackness and want of vigour.

clue.text: What may be trained as pet within year?

definitions.text: What may be trained as pet within year?

indicators.note: within means inside, so the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: yr is the abbreviation for year

indicators.note: trained means drilled into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that can be house-trained as a pet within a year: a puppy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A yapster is a dog, especially a small yapping one, the kind of animal one trains as a pet.

clue.text: Meat's cooked in ale — maybe I'll produce honey

indicators.note: in places the reworked letters inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A cook stews meat in ale and boasts of making honey too.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken in the first person: the beekeeper is the one saying it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beemaster is an old word for a beekeeper, whose hives produce honey.

clue.text: Awful noise once from musician, less flat at edges

indicators.note: less means minus, so letters of the following word are taken away
at edges says the removed letters come from the two ends of the word, not its middle

parts.note: a flautist is a musician who plays the flute
taken as written, the letters to be removed from the ends

explanation.surface: A dreadful racket comes from a player who is no longer playing flat.
explanation.walkthrough: FLA comes off the front of the musician and T off the back, which together spell the removed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an old Shakespearean word for a din, uproar or noisy merriment.

clue.text: Form of gene detectable in small elephants

indicators.note: detectable in means it can be spotted inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A gene variant can be found in small elephants, as in a genetics study.
explanation.definitionFit: An allele is one of the alternative versions of a gene found at a given chromosome position.

clue.text: Bodice showing frilly ties etc round border

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the last item
frilly suggests ruffled and gathered, so the letters are ruffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
a hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A bodice is decorated with frilly ties and trimmings around its border.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemisette is a woman's bodice-like garment or lace insert filling the neckline of a dress.

clue.text: Work in garden interrupted by fuss over harmless snake

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing breaking into its middle

parts.note: to hoe is to work the soil of a garden

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a song, as in song and dance, is a fuss

explanation.surface: Gardening is disturbed by a commotion over a snake that turns out to be harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a song about' something means fussing over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hognose is a North American snake with an upturned snout, harmless to people despite its bluffing.

clue.text: Crazy (if not OTT), like Nero — first clue, maybe, …

definitions.text: Crazy (if not OTT), like Nero — first clue, maybe, …

indicators.note: if not here means without, so the named letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy
taken as written, the letters to be dropped
Nero was a Roman emperor
1ac is crossword shorthand for the first across clue, with the digit read as the letter I; maybe because this grid has no 1 across

explanation.surface: Nero is called mad, if not over the top, in what runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into 26 across: Nero, the fire-raiser of legend, fiddled while Rome burned. OTT is short for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyromaniac has a compulsion to start fires, as Nero was popularly said to have set Rome alight.

clue.text: E.g. chicken cut up, obstruction being small bone

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters read from bottom to top
cut here means docked, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a chicken is an example of a bird
let is an old word for hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A cut-up chicken has a small bone that gets stuck, as in a carving mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like one phrase about carving, but cut docks the word and up reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A riblet is a small rib, and ribs are among the small bones of a carcase.

clue.text: Poem's modified after one command (in Shakespeare)

indicators.note: after says the reworked letters come behind the single one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A poem has been revised after someone's command, a note on Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare impose is used as a noun meaning a command or charge laid upon someone.

clue.text: Former fashion is limited by fit

indicators.note: something limited by another is bounded on both sides, so it goes inside

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever or shivering
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion that has passed is restricted by what fits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb here, not a noun: an old word for to shape or dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Aguise is a Spenserian verb meaning to dress, adorn or fashion, now obsolete.

clue.text: … Playing this (dress in fashion)?

definitions.note: with the previous clue: what Nero is said to have played while Rome burned

indicators.note: in places one part inside the other

parts.note: ton is the prevailing fashion or style
to rig out is to dress

explanation.surface: Read on from the previous clue, Nero is playing an instrument while dressed fashionably.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 22 across: Nero fiddled while Rome burned, and this is the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A trigon is an ancient triangular lyre or harp, a fitting stand-in for Nero's fiddle.

clue.text: Old stone to polish on the spot

parts.note: to rub is to polish
in as in in situ, present at the place

explanation.surface: An antique gem is polished on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubin is an obsolete form of ruby, the red precious stone.

clue.text: What's à la plage, seen drifting, bits regularly detached?

definitions.text: What's à la plage, seen drifting, bits regularly detached?

indicators.note: drifting things float about and lose their order, so the kept letters are rearranged
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Something found at the beach is seen drifting, with bits broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: À la plage is French for at the beach. The whole clue is both wordplay and a description of seaweed washed up on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: An alga is a simple water plant, such as seaweed, often found drifting at the seaside.

clue.text: Tailor I consult has this for lining leather cuirass

indicators.note: the words before carry the result inside them as a lining, so it lies within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A tailor consulted about lining a leather breastplate.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorica, or loric, was a Roman cuirass, originally made of leather, protecting the torso.

clue.text: Axeman denied aspiration in jug

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy sound written as H, so denying it drops that letter

parts.note: a hewer chops wood or stone with an axe

explanation.surface: A woodcutter whose ambitions are thwarted ends up in jug, slang for prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' looks like ambition, but it is the sound of H, and 'in jug' suggests jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large pitcher or jug, traditionally used to carry washing water.

clue.text: Refusenik with devout following in plentiful numbers

indicators.note: following says the second part comes after the first

parts.note: a CO is a conscientious objector, one who refuses military service
pious means devout

explanation.surface: Objectors and their devout followers turn out in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means abundant or plentiful, existing in large quantities.

clue.text: One to show reverence about lecturer, spouting?

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the gesture goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to bow is to show reverence
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: Someone bows respectfully before a lecturer who is spouting forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spouting' suggests a windbag lecturer, but the question mark points to a whale blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablow means in a blowing state, as a whale is when it spouts water from its blowhole.

clue.text: Summons involving squaddies, cause for concern locally

indicators.note: involving means wrapping up within itself, so the second part goes inside the first

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A summons served on some soldiers gives cause for worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Squaddies are British army privates, the other ranks, abbreviated OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Worrit is a dialect word for worry or anxiety, a source of concern in regional speech.

clue.text: Loco maybe stops working on raised tracks

indicators.note: on says the first part is joined directly onto the second

parts.note: an engine that dies stops working
an el is an American elevated railway

explanation.surface: A locomotive breaks down on an elevated railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a reversal signal, but the el is simply the elevated railway, as in Chicago.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive powered by a diesel engine, so one example of a loco.

clue.text: Lawyer's put in possession of part of case I settle

indicators.note: part of means a piece taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A lawyer talks of having part of a case settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawyer's' means in legal language, not belonging to a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to seise someone is to give them possession of land, a legal term of art.

clue.text: Translate bit of poetry engraved inside fashionable ring

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: engraved inside means cut into the inner surface, so one letter goes within the ring

parts.note: a terret is a ring on a harness through which the reins pass

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone translates a line of verse engraved inside a stylish ring.
explanation.walkthrough: A terret is a metal ring on horse harness that guides the reins.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to render words from one language into another, as a translator does.
